title: Explicit quotient-Jacobian minor formulas for formal coordinates
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $n,s\geq0$, $T=F[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] together with an $F$-algebra coordinate isomorphism $F[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]]\xrightarrow{\sim}T$, $Y_k\mapsto y_k$. Let $I\subseteq T$ be any ideal, $\pi:T\to R=T/I$ the quotient map, and $h_1,\ldots,h_s\in T$ any finite list. Use termwise formal partial derivatives in the indicated coordinates [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Set $Q=(\partial y_k/\partial x_i)_{k,i}$ and $P=(\partial x_i/\partial y_k)_{i,k}$ over $T$ [def-weil-matrix], and define the $s\times n$ quotient Jacobians $H_x=(\pi(\partial h_j/\partial x_i))_{j,i}$ and $H_y=(\pi(\partial h_j/\partial y_k))_{j,k}$. Then $QP=PQ=1_n$, and, writing bars for entrywise reduction modulo $I$,
$$\overline Q\,\overline P=\overline P\,\overline Q=1_n,\qquad H_x=H_y\overline Q,\qquad H_y=H_x\overline P.$$
For every $r\geq0$ and subsets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}$, $B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of cardinality $r$, all ordered increasingly, one has in $R$
$$\det((H_x)_{A,B})=\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\\|S|=r}}\det((H_y)_{A,S})\det(\overline Q_{S,B}),$$
$$\det((H_y)_{A,B})=\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\\|S|=r}}\det((H_x)_{A,S})\det(\overline P_{S,B}).$$
Submatrices and determinants mean [def-weil-submatrix] and [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Empty determinants equal $1$, so $r=0$ and $n=0$ are included. No stability of $I$ under the coordinate isomorphism is assumed: both Jacobians are reduced modulo the same ideal of $T$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-coordinate-chain-rule] to the given $F$-algebra coordinate isomorphism and parameters. Its hypotheses are exactly those on $F,T,y$ here. Its inverse matrix is the specified $P$, so $QP=PQ=1_n$. For each $h_j$, its two chain rules give
$$\partial_{x_i}h_j=\sum_k(\partial_{y_k}h_j)Q_{ki},\qquad
\partial_{y_k}h_j=\sum_i(\partial_{x_i}h_j)P_{ik}.$$
These are identities in $T$, before taking any quotient.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), coordinate-change paragraph: invertible coordinate Jacobian and chain rule; quotient reduction, inverse formula, and the two selected-minor expansions; selected-minor formula made explicit using algebra.tex Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet).

proof.text:
Apply the ring homomorphism $\pi$ to these finite sums and products. Entrywise,
$$\pi(\partial_{x_i}h_j)=\sum_k\pi(\partial_{y_k}h_j)\pi(Q_{ki}),\qquad
\pi(\partial_{y_k}h_j)=\sum_i\pi(\partial_{x_i}h_j)\pi(P_{ik}),$$
which give $H_x=H_y\overline Q$ and $H_y=H_x\overline P$. Likewise $\pi(\sum_k Q_{ak}P_{kb})=\sum_k\pi(Q_{ak})\pi(P_{kb})=\delta_{ab}$, and the reversed product gives $\overline P\overline Q=1_n$. This uses only the quotient homomorphism of the fixed ideal $I$, never an induced coordinate automorphism of $T/I$.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), coordinate-change paragraph: invertible coordinate Jacobian and chain rule; quotient reduction, inverse formula, and the two selected-minor expansions; selected-minor formula made explicit using algebra.tex Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet).

proof.text:
Fix the increasing enumerations $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ and $B=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$. By [def-weil-submatrix] put $M=(H_y)_{A,\{1,\ldots,n\}}$ and $N=\overline Q_{\{1,\ldots,n\},B}$, of sizes $r\times n$ and $n\times r$. For $1\leq u,v\leq r$,
$$(MN)_{uv}=\sum_{k=1}^n(H_y)_{a_u k}\overline Q_{kb_v}=(H_x)_{a_u b_v}.$$
Thus $MN=(H_x)_{A,B}$. Replacing $(H_y,\overline Q,H_x)$ with $(H_x,\overline P,H_y)$ gives the analogous factorization of $(H_y)_{A,B}$.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), coordinate-change paragraph: invertible coordinate Jacobian and chain rule; quotient reduction, inverse formula, and the two selected-minor expansions; selected-minor formula made explicit using algebra.tex Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] over the commutative ring $R=T/I$ to the two rectangular factorizations in Step 3, with its $m=r$. In the first factorization its column-selected matrix is $(H_y)_{A,S}$ and its row-selected matrix is $\overline Q_{S,B}$; both use the same increasing enumeration of $S$. Hence its determinant formula is exactly the first required sum. For the second factorization the two selected matrices are $(H_x)_{A,S}$ and $\overline P_{S,B}$, giving the second required sum. No permutation of $A,B$ or $S$ is introduced.

source.place: Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet), applied to the row/column-selected rectangular factors from Curves Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined).

proof.text: For $r=0$, the only size-zero subset is empty, and [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives value $1$ for all three empty determinants in either expansion; the sums are $1\cdot1=1$. If $n=0$, a subset $B$ as in the statement forces $r=0$, and all square coordinate matrices are the unique empty matrix. If $s=0$ the same conclusion follows from $A$. For $r>\min(s,n)$ no such $A,B$ exist. The identities also hold for $I=T$: $R$ is then the zero ring, where $1=0$.
